headline: High: Perplexity’s browser-backed search output can be treated as authoritative by social-auto-upload, creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse live web content and produce cited answers, while social-auto-upload is a CLI uploader that can consume generated content for posting. The pair has a plausible content-to-action bridge, but no shared filesystem or MCP channel is documented, so this is not high. The risk is that web-sourced text from A is reused by B without provenance checks.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a output as post text or captions without sanitization
IF agent_a returns web-derived instructions that agent_b forwards into upload metadata
mitigations: Add a manual review step before upload
Strip instructions and URLs from A output before passing to B
Use a fixed caption template in B
Log source provenance for each uploaded field
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded documents and browsing context, and B touches account data plus media files. There is no documented shared workspace, same OAuth principal, or filesystem bridge, so leakage is not default-path. The main exposure is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive document content from A into B’s upload workflow.
conditions: IF the operator copies uploaded document content from agent_a into agent_b upload assets
IF agent_b is used to publish media containing sensitive material first surfaced in agent_a
mitigations: Avoid passing documents from A into B
Redact sensitive fields before upload
Use separate accounts for each agent
Check upload folders for secrets before posting
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write-adjacent effects on mutable external resources, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or shared mutable storage. Per the rubric, overlap is limited to external service actions and account/media handling, so direct capability conflict is small and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external account or upload destination
IF the operator reuses the same media directory across runs
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Run one upload job at a time
Keep distinct accounts per agent
Disable concurrent edits to shared assets
requires-engineering: add locking for shared destinations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity’s cited answers can be treated as authoritative inputs, and social-auto-upload is designed to act on prepared media and metadata. That creates a default-path cascade if B forwards A’s output without verification. The blast radius is multiple posts or account actions, but not clearly irreversible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a text as final post copy without human verification
IF agent_a’s citations are not checked before upload
mitigations: Require human approval of A output
Compare A claims against source links before posting
Use a checklist for each upload
Limit B to draft mode until reviewed
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-hosted search/RAG with uploaded documents and browsing context, while B is a social-media uploader handling account data and media. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data classes and posting workflows rather than a proven policy conflict.
conditions: IF uploaded documents in agent_a contain regulated data that are then published via agent_b
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two services for the same media
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through A
Review each service’s retention policy
Use non-sensitive test content
Delete temporary upload artifacts after posting
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
